title: Building a JSON document by string concatenation of unknown input
purpose: Prevent corrupt JSON (broken quotes, mangled newlines/backslash) that a machine consumer then mis-parses, which is a frequent LLM-authored bash failure when the value can contain quotes or control characters.
trigger: A JSON document is assembled by concatenating unescaped variables into a quoted string (for example printf '"a":"%s"' "$v" where v is not first escaped) instead of escaping with the field-appropriate helper or serializing with a JSON engine.
correct: If the value is fixed and known-safe, run it through a backslash-first escape helper; otherwise pass the raw arguments to a Python heredoc that calls json.dumps. Never concatenate an unescaped unknown value into a JSON string.
evidence_note: Grounded in queuebash.sh default escape helper and the python-heredoc json.dumps path in bin/queue-vcs-probe; docs/QUEUE_COMMAND_CONTRACT.md keeps JSON parseable on stdout.
return_semantics: A reference rule page; shown for LLM author guidance, not executed by rules check.
